PesqueiroArruda.TITLE: Pesqueiro Arruda's — Restaurant & Reservations Platform
PesqueiroArruda.SUBTITLE: A real, in-production system for a family-run fishing resort & restaurant — designed and built solo, alongside a full-time job.
PesqueiroArruda.OVERVIEW: Pesqueiro Arruda's is a fishing resort and restaurant run by my family. I designed and built the software that runs its daily operations and its public-facing booking site, and I still maintain both today.
PesqueiroArruda.PROBLEM: Before the system existed, orders and tabs were tracked on paper, stock wasn't tracked digitally, and there was no way for guests to reserve a table or pay a deposit online.
PesqueiroArruda.SYSTEMS_INTRO: Three connected systems, each deployed and evolving on its own.

BACKEND.TITLE: Backend
BACKEND.STACK: Node.js, Express, MongoDB, Socket.IO, JWT, AWS S3
BACKEND.DESCRIPTION: The API and single source of truth for products, stock, orders and payments. Socket.IO pushes real-time updates to every connected client; JWT protects the API; media is stored on AWS S3.

ADMIN.TITLE: Operations app
ADMIN.STACK: Next.js, TypeScript, Chakra UI, Socket.IO, dnd-kit
ADMIN.DESCRIPTION: Used by staff on the floor, in the kitchen and at the register. Handles order tabs, a live kitchen queue, checkout and stock, with drag-and-drop reordering. Talks to the backend over REST and Socket.IO, so a new order appears in the kitchen instantly.

SITE.TITLE: Public site
SITE.STACK: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, InfinitePay, Resend, Zod
SITE.DESCRIPTION: Online table reservations and deposit payments via InfinitePay, with Zod validation and email confirmations through Resend.

DECISIONS.TITLE: Webhook, but verify server-side
DECISIONS.DESCRIPTION: InfinitePay confirms a deposit via webhook, but the backend re-confirms the payment directly against InfinitePay's API before marking a reservation as paid — a webhook payload alone isn't trusted.

DECISIONS.TITLE: Real-time over polling
DECISIONS.DESCRIPTION: Kitchen and register run on Socket.IO so every device reflects the current state of an order immediately, instead of refreshing or polling the API.

DECISIONS.TITLE: One source of truth for the catalog
DECISIONS.DESCRIPTION: The public site doesn't keep its own copy of the menu — the digital menu (in progress) reads products directly from the operational backend, so stock and pricing can't drift between systems.

DECISIONS.TITLE: Three deployables, one system
DECISIONS.DESCRIPTION: Splitting the internal operations app from the public site means staff-facing features ship without touching the public site's uptime, and vice versa.

PesqueiroArruda.RESULT: In daily use by staff to run the floor, kitchen and register, and by guests to reserve tables and pay deposits online.
PesqueiroArruda.NEXT_STEPS: A digital menu embedded in the public site, synced live with the backend's product catalog — spec already written, implementation in progress.
